Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: The first wave registers canonical and mechanistically plausible dependencies in a lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dataset. More negative dependency scores indicate stronger dependency, so most hypotheses use negative directions to represent stronger dependency in the exposed/aberrant group. The selected comparisons cover pathway drivers (KRAS mutation for KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E for BRAF dependency, EGFR or ERBB2 amplification for receptor-tyrosine kinase dependencies), synthetic-lethal tumor-suppressor relationships (TP53 wild-type vs loss for MDM2; KEAP1 loss for NFE2L2; SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2), and known or plausible DNA damage/repair dependencies in MSI-high cancers (WRN and DHX9). MYC amplification is included for POLR2A because transcriptional amplification may increase transcriptional machinery dependency. Interaction claims test whether KRAS and EGFR dependencies are stronger within adenocarcinoma than in the complement lineage subtype. For the negative mean dependency scores, a clinically meaningful 10% relative difference corresponds roughly to a 0.025 absolute score shift around the observed -0.25 means, though I will judge each result against the comparator mean and uncertainty. All claims begin unresolved.

Iteration 1/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: The independent validation for H4 does not support accepting EGFR amplification as associated with stronger EGFR dependency. The discovery estimate was borderline relative to the 10% clinical threshold (signed effect +0.0252, 95% interval -0.0003 to +0.0507), but the validation estimate is near zero (+0.0015) with a wide adjusted interval (-0.0431 to +0.0461) that includes both no effect and effects larger than the threshold. I therefore leave H4 unresolved as an association that is not accepted, but close it because the available independent validation does not motivate additional analysis of the same main contrast. The KEAP1/NFE2L2 result is now best expressed as the reversed claim H13: KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less negative dependency_NFE2L2 scores, with a raw signed effect of about +0.80 (95% interval +0.78 to +0.82). This is a very large association far exceeding the clinical-significance scale, so I accept H13 and close the original rejected H8. The strong accepted findings remain SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency and MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency. The next wave focuses on whether robust associations are subtype-driven, whether chromatin-remodeler relationships extend to ARID1A co-loss, whether other DNA repair or p53 pathway dependencies emerge, and whether unassigned research markers explain additional dependency variation. These are dataset associations, not causal claims.

record.narrative: These proposals extend the currently accepted dataset associations rather than repeating them. The KEAP1/NFE2L2 reversed association is now registered in the correct direction in H13; the new interaction and library-restricted claims ask whether it is stronger in adenocarcinoma, whether it remains large in the dominant Avana screen library, and whether it is robust across measured screening context. Similarly, SMARCA4-loss-driven SMARCA2 dependency is tested for lineage heterogeneity and Avana-library robustness. MSI-high association with WRN is also checked within Avana, while additional DNA-repair hypotheses (BRCA2 loss with WRN/DHX9 and MSI-high with USP7) broaden the DNA damage response exploration. Reciprocal receptor-tyrosine-kinase hypotheses test amplification-specific cross dependencies: EGFR amplification associated with weaker ERBB2 dependency and ERBB2 amplification associated with weaker EGFR dependency. Finally, two unassigned marker claims probe whether research marker D or F predicts SMARCA2 or WRN dependency; their expected raw direction is deliberately uncertain, with the registered direction testing stronger dependency.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: I requested 12 previously registered, untested comparisons selected to allocate investigation across focused follow-up and broad discovery. The focused set tests whether accepted dataset associations are lineage-specific or library-specific: adenocarcinoma KEAP1/NFE2L2 and adenocarcinoma MSI/WRN, and Avana-library-restricted SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 contrasts. The mechanistic set tests additional synthetic-lethal or pathway hypotheses: ARID1A loss for SMARCA2 dependency and SMARCA4 loss interaction with ARID1A loss; TP53 wild-type status for USP7 and RPL11 dependencies; BRCA2 loss for WRN dependency; and MSI-high for USP7 dependency. The marker set probes unassigned research assays, especially marker D with SMARCA2 and marker F with WRN/DHX9, because these may reveal additional associations even if they lack assigned biological roles. These are dataset-level associations; no causal inference or independent validation is implied.

Iteration 2/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: This wave mostly confirms earlier strong associations and identifies one new strong association. H20 and H21 show that the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 and MSI-high/WRN effects remain very large and precise within adenocarcinoma. H35 and H36 show the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 effects remain essentially unchanged when restricted to the dominant Avana screen library. These are accepted as dataset-level robustness confirmations; they do not establish causality or generalizability beyond this dataset. H14, H16, H42, and H43 do not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency: the point estimates are near zero or opposite, and the maximum claimed-direction interval support is below the approximate 10% relative-scale threshold for these outcomes, so they are rejected and closed. H22 is an ARID1A co-loss interaction on the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association; the point estimate is in the hypothesized direction but is small and imprecise, so it is unresolved and deferred rather than accepted. H37 is near null for BRCA2 loss and WRN dependency; although its wide interval includes some clinically meaningful negative values, the point estimate is essentially zero, so it is unresolved and closed. H39 is borderline: the signed estimate suggests MSI-high may have stronger USP7 dependency and the point estimate is plausibly meaningful, but the interval crosses null and could be confounded by p53 status, mutation burden, or screening context; it remains unresolved and active. H15 is the main new finding: TP53 wild-type versus TP53-loss cells show a raw USP7 dependency difference of about -0.396 (reported signed +0.396), with a narrow interval far above the clinical threshold and biologically plausible because wild-type p53 pathway states may increase USP7 dependency. I accept H15 and request independent validation because it is a new, large, pathway-level association and independent confirmation would be scientifically useful. Multiplicity and confounding remain concerns: these are unadjusted Welch comparisons in a cross-sectional cell-line dataset, and predictors may correlate with screen library, batch, growth pattern, ploidy, or mutation burden. I registered H15 stratification analyses in Avana, adenocarcinoma, and adherent culture, plus a USP7-MSI analysis restricted to TP53 wild-type cells, to test whether the new USP7 effect and the borderline MSI-USP7 signal are robust or confounded.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The independent validation for H15 strongly supports the TP53 wild-type/USP7 dependency association. Discovery evidence R15 gives a signed effect of +0.396 with 95% interval +0.325 to +0.467, and independent validation R26 gives +0.394 with a more conservative independent interval +0.290 to +0.498. The estimates are nearly identical, and the validation interval remains far above zero and above the approximate 10% clinically meaningful scale for this outcome. Therefore, within this supplied dataset, TP53 wild-type status is associated with stronger USP7 dependency relative to TP53-loss status. I accept H15 and close investigation of the main contrast because discovery plus independent validation have now settled that registered comparison. This is not a causal claim: TP53 loss is a measured cellular feature, but TP53 pathway state may be correlated with other genomic, copy-number, ploidy, mutation-burden, library, batch, or culture factors. The registered refinements H44-H47 test the TP53-WT/USP7 effect in the dominant Avana screen library, in adenocarcinoma, in adherent culture, and test whether the borderline MSI-high/USP7 signal is robust within TP53 wild-type cells; these are separate from the validated main contrast. The additional interaction proposals probe whether accepted synthetic-lethal-like associations are modified by co-occurring genomic states: KEAP1/NFE2L2 by KRAS mutation, SMARCA4/SMARCA2 by TP53 loss, MSI/WRN by KRAS mutation, and TP53/USP7 by KEAP1 loss. These remain dataset associations and may fail if subgroup cells are small or effects are context-dependent.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

H35 and H36 show the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 effects remain essentially unchanged when restricted to the dominant Avana screen library. These are accepted as dataset-level robustness confirmations; they do not establish causality or generalizability beyond this dataset. H14, H16, H42, and H43 do not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency: the point estimates are near zero or opposite, and the maximum claimed-direction interval support is below the approximate 10% relative-scale threshold for these outcomes, so they are rejected and closed. H22 is an ARID1A co-loss interaction on the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association; the point estimate is in the hypothesized direction but is small and imprecise, so it is unresolved and deferred rather than accepted. H37 is near null for BRCA2 loss and WRN dependency; although its wide interval includes some clinically meaningful negative values, the point estimate is essentially zero, so it is unresolved and closed. H39 is borderline: the signed estimate suggests MSI-high may have stronger USP7 dependency and the point estimate is plausibly meaningful, but the interval crosses null and could be confounded by p53 status, mutation burden, or screening context; it remains unresolved and active. H15 is the main new finding: TP53 wild-type versus TP53-loss cells show a raw USP7 dependency difference of about -0.396 (reported signed +0.396), with a narrow interval far above the clinical threshold and biologically plausible because wild-type p53 pathway states may increase USP7 dependency. record.narrative: These new comparisons are focused refinements of the strongest accepted dataset associations. The goal is not to repeat the main effects, but to ask whether they persist after imposing biologically important contexts that could plausibly confound or modify them. For SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency, I registered adenocarcinoma, ARID1A-wild-type, and low-mutation-burden restrictions to test whether the synthetic-lethal-like association is merely lineage-driven, ARID1A-co-loss-driven, or mutation-burden-driven. For KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency, I registered adherent-culture and TP53-wild-type restrictions because the main reversed association is very large but may be sensitive to culture context or p53 co-alteration. For MSI-high/WRN dependency, I registered adherent-culture and TP53-wild-type restrictions to test whether the association is robust to culture and independent of p53 loss. For TP53 wild-type/USP7 dependency, I registered high-mutation-burden and KEAP1-wild-type restrictions because TP53 loss correlates with other pathway states and may be correlated with mutation burden or KEAP1 co-alteration. The expected directions follow the accepted claims: stronger dependency for SMARCA2, WRN, and USP7, and weaker/higher NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss. If these context-restricted estimates remain large and precise, they will support robust dataset-level associations; if they attenuate, that will motivate interaction or confounding-focused follow-up. These are still associations in a cross-sectional cell-line dataset, not causal claims.

record.narrative:
This wave largely establishes robustness of the main accepted dataset associations across several biologically relevant contexts. H52-H54 restrict SMARCA4-loss versus non-loss for SMARCA2 dependency to adenocarcinoma, ARID1A-wild-type cells, and low-mutation-burden cells. In all three restrictions, the signed effect remains about +0.77 to +0.78 with narrow intervals far from zero. This argues against the simple explanations that the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association is driven only by lineage, ARID1A co-loss, or low mutation burden. I therefore accept H52-H54 as dataset-level robustness confirmations and close those investigations.

H55-H56 restrict KEAP1-loss versus non-loss for NFE2L2 dependency to adherent culture and TP53-wild-type cells. The signed effects remain about +0.79 with tight intervals, showing that the large KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association persists after these potential context or co-alteration restrictions. These are accepted and closed. H57-H58 restrict MSI-high versus non-MSI-high for WRN dependency to adherent culture and TP53-wild-type cells; the signed effects remain about +0.78 to +0.81 and precise. H34 additionally shows the MSI/WRN effect remains essentially unchanged within the dominant Avana screen library. Thus the MSI/WRN association is not merely a culture artifact, TP53-loss artifact, or Avana-library-specific screening artifact. These are accepted and closed.

For USP7, H44 shows the validated TP53-wild-type/TP53-loss association remains robust within the Avana library, with a signed effect about +0.40. This supports H44 and closes it. H59 restricts the TP53-wild-type/USP7 contrast to high mutation burden and yields a larger signed effect, about +0.48, with a precise interval well above clinical relevance. H60 restricts the contrast to KEAP1-wild-type cells and yields a signed effect about +0.37, also well above clinical relevance. These results suggest that the TP53-wild-type/USP7 association is robust to screening library and KEAP1 state and may be even stronger in higher mutation-burden contexts. I accept H60 and close it. I accept H59 but keep it active and request independent validation because it is a context-specific refinement with a large new point estimate; independent confirmation would be useful before closing it as a separate context association. This is not a causal claim: high mutation burden may correlate with MSI, DNA-repair defects, p53 pathway state, aneuploidy, or screening/context factors, and the observed modification could be confounded or biologically context dependent.

H47 tests whether the borderline MSI-high/USP7 signal survives within TP53-wild-type cells. The signed estimate is only +0.032 and the interval crosses zero, [-0.003, +0.068]. The point estimate is much smaller than the main accepted associations, and the uncertainty is insufficient to support a clinically meaningful MSI-high/USP7 association. Combined with the earlier borderline H39 result, I leave H47 unresolved but close it, and I close H39 as well to reduce low-priority follow-up. The evidence does not support accepting MSI-high as a robust predictor of USP7 dependency in this dataset.

Overall, the strongest conclusions remain dataset-level associations: SMARCA4 loss associates with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss associates with weaker/higher NFE2L2 dependency; MSI-high associates with stronger WRN dependency; and TP53-wild-type status associates with stronger USP7 dependency. The new results make these effects much less attributable to lineage subtype, ARID1A co-loss, low mutation burden, culture type, TP53-loss co-state, Avana library, or KEAP1 co-state. Residual confounding remains possible due to unmeasured pathway interactions, batch, screen quality, growth rate, media, ploidy, or co-alteration structure, and no result should be interpreted as causality or external generalizability.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The newly released validation evidence substantially sharpens the conclusion for USP7 and confirms that the main EGFR-amplification claim is not supported. H4 tested whether EGFR amplification is associated with stronger EGFR dependency. The discovery result was already weak: the signed estimate was only +0.025 and its lower bound touched zero. Independent validation is essentially null, with a signed estimate of +0.0015 and an independent interval spanning both sides of zero. There is no reproducible evidence of a clinically meaningful EGFR-dependency effect in this dataset, so I reject H4 and close it. This is a negative conclusion for the registered EGFR-amplification contrast, not proof that EGFR copy-number states never affect dependency; amplification may be a poor proxy for functional EGFR pathway activity or may be confounded by co-amplified loci.  H36 tests KEAP1 loss versus non-loss for NFE2L2 dependency restricted to the dominant Avana screen library. Discovery and independent validation are nearly identical, with signed effects of about +0.796 and +0.795 and tight intervals far above clinical relevance. I accept and close H36. This strongly argues that the large KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is not merely an Avana-library artifact within this dataset.  H59 tests TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss for USP7 dependency restricted to higher mutation burden. Discovery gave a signed effect of +0.477, and independent validation gave +0.392 with an interval +0.239 to +0.545. Although the point estimate attenuates in validation, it remains far above clinically meaningful thresholds and in the same direction as the main TP53 wild-type/USP7 association. I therefore accept and close H59 as a robust dataset-level context confirmation. The attenuation is a useful caveat: TP53-loss cells and high mutation burden are biologically heterogeneous, and mutation burden may correlate with MSI, DNA-repair defects, p53 pathway state, aneuploidy, or screening artifacts. Thus the claim is that higher-mutation-burden cells in this dataset still show the TP53 wild-type/USP7 association, not that mutation burden causally amplifies USP7 dependency.  Overall, the accepted main dataset associations remain: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker/higher NFE2L2 dependency; MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency; and TP53 wild-type with stronger USP7 dependency. The USP7 association is now validated both overall and in the higher-mutation-burden context, and the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is validated in the dominant screen library. The next priority is to validate or robustness-test the remaining accepted main effects, especially SMARCA4/SMARCA2 and MSI/WRN, while continuing to explore modification by co-alterations and context.

Negative or low-priority findings: EGFR amplification, BRAF V600E/BRAF dependency, ARID1A/SMARCA2, TP53 loss/RPL11, TP53 wild-type/MDM2, MSI/DHX9, MYC/POLR2A, MSI/USP7, and several marker claims are not accepted; many are null or borderline rather than definitive absence. Robustness already accepted for main effects: SMARCA4/SMARCA2 in adenocarcinoma, ARID1A wild-type, and low mutation burden; KEAP1/NFE2L2 in adherent culture, TP53 wild-type, and Avana; MSI/WRN in adenocarcinoma, adherent culture, TP53 wild-type, and Avana; TP53 wild-type/USP7 in Avana and KEAP1 wild-type. Next appraise priority: request independent validation for H9 SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 dependency, then H10 MSI/WRN or H13 KEAP1/NFE2L2 if useful. Analyze should test new robustness proposals: USP7 low mutation burden and batch_a; main effects in batch_a; SMARCA2 and NFE2L2 in higher mutation burden. Also test existing interactions H48-H51 and pending broad marker/gene discoveries. Interpret all findings as dataset-level associations, not causal inference or external generalizability. Context restrictions reduce some confounding candidates but cannot exclude batch, screen quality, ploidy, growth rate, media, DNA/RNA omics availability, or correlated genomic states.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"These new comparisons are focused refinements of the strongest accepted dataset associations. The goal is not to repeat the main effects, but to ask whether they persist after imposing biologically important contexts that could plausibly confound or modify them. For SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency, I registered adenocarcinoma, ARID1A-wild-type, and low-mutation-burden restrictions to test whether the synthetic-lethal-like association is merely lineage-driven, ARID1A-co-loss-driven, or mutation-burden-driven. For KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency, I registered adherent-culture and TP53-wild-type restrictions because the main reversed association is very large but may be sensitive to culture context or p53 co-alteration. For MSI-high/WRN dependency, I registered adherent-culture and TP53-wild-type restrictions to test whether the association is robust to culture and independent of p53 loss. For TP53 wild-type/USP7 dependency, I registered high-mutation-burden and KEAP1-wild-type restrictions because TP53 loss correlates with other pathway states and may be correlated with mutation burden or KEAP1 co-alteration. The expected directions follow the accepted claims: stronger dependency for SMARCA2, WRN, and USP7, and weaker/higher NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss. If these context-restricted estimates remain large and precise, they will support robust dataset-level associations; if they attenuate, that will motivate interaction or confounding-focused follow-up. These are still associations in a cross-sectional cell-line dataset, not causal claims.","analyze":"I selected 12 untested existing claims to test robustness and possible confounding of the strongest accepted dataset associations while completing the most useful pending follow-ups. H52-H60 are the newly registered context restrictions: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 within adenocarcinoma, ARID1A wild-type, and low mutation burden; KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 within adherent culture and TP53 wild-type; MSI-high/WRN within adherent culture and TP53 wild-type; and TP53 wild-type/USP7 within high mutation burden and KEAP1 wild-type. These ask whether the large effects are merely driven by lineage, co-alterations, mutation burden, culture context, or p53/KEAP1 co-state. I also included H34 and H44 to test whether the MSI-high/WRN and TP53 wild-type/USP7 associations remain in the dominant Avana screen library, because screening-library artifacts or library-specific screen quality could otherwise explain accepted effects. Finally, H47 tests whether the borderline MSI-high/USP7 signal remains within TP53 wild-type cells, separating a possible independent DNA-repair/MSS pathway association from confounding by TP53 state. This batch is deliberately focused on accepted or borderline accepted effects and likely confounders, rather than low-priority marker or reciprocal RTK broad exploration.","appraise":"This wave largely establishes robustness of the main accepted dataset associations across several biologically relevant contexts. H52-H54 restrict SMARCA4-loss versus non-loss for SMARCA2 dependency to adenocarcinoma, ARID1A-wild-type cells, and low-mutation-burden cells. In all three restrictions, the signed effect remains about +0.77 to +0.78 with narrow intervals far from zero. This argues against the simple explanations that the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association is driven only by lineage, ARID1A co-loss, or low mutation burden. I therefore accept H52-H54 as dataset-level robustness confirmations and close those investigations.\n\nH55-H56 restrict KEAP1-loss versus non-loss for NFE2L2 dependency to adherent culture and TP53-wild-type cells. The signed effects remain about +0.79 with tight intervals, showing that the large KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association persists after these potential context or co-alteration restrictions. These are accepted and closed. H57-H58 restrict MSI-high versus non-MSI-high for WRN dependency to adherent culture and TP53-wild-type cells; the signed effects remain about +0.78 to +0.81 and precise. H34 additionally shows the MSI/WRN effect remains essentially unchanged within the dominant Avana screen library. Thus the MSI/WRN association is not merely a culture artifact, TP53-loss artifact, or Avana-library-specific screening artifact. These are accepted and closed.\n\nFor USP7, H44 shows the validated TP53-wild-type/TP53-loss association remains robust within the Avana library, with a signed effect about +0.40. This supports H44 and closes it. H59 restricts the TP53-wild-type/USP7 contrast to high mutation burden and yields a larger signed effect, about +0.48, with a precise interval well above clinical relevance. H60 restricts the contrast to KEAP1-wild-type cells and yields a signed effect about +0.37, also well above clinical relevance. These results suggest that the TP53-wild-type/USP7 association is robust to screening library and KEAP1 state and may be even stronger in higher mutation-burden contexts. I accept H60 and close it. I accept H59 but keep it active and request independent validation because it is a context-specific refinement with a large new point estimate; independent confirmation would be useful before closing it as a separate context association. This is not a causal claim: high mutation burden may correlate with MSI, DNA-repair defects, p53 pathway state, aneuploidy, or screening/context factors, and the observed modification could be confounded or biologically context dependent.\n\nH47 tests whether the borderline MSI-high/USP7 signal survives within TP53-wild-type cells. The signed estimate is only +0.032 and the interval crosses zero, [-0.003, +0.068]. The point estimate is much smaller than the main accepted associations, and the uncertainty is insufficient to support a clinically meaningful MSI-high/USP7 association. Combined with the earlier borderline H39 result, I leave H47 unresolved but close it, and I close H39 as well to reduce low-priority follow-up. The evidence does not support accepting MSI-high as a robust predictor of USP7 dependency in this dataset.\n\nOverall, the strongest conclusions remain dataset-level associations: SMARCA4 loss associates with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss associates with weaker/higher NFE2L2 dependency; MSI-high associates with stronger WRN dependency; and TP53-wild-type status associates with stronger USP7 dependency. The new results make these effects much less attributable to lineage subtype, ARID1A co-loss, low mutation burden, culture type, TP53-loss co-state, Avana library, or KEAP1 co-state. Residual confounding remains possible due to unmeasured pathway interactions, batch, screen quality, growth rate, media, ploidy, or co-alteration structure, and no result should be interpreted as causality or external generalizability.","synthesize":"The newly released validation evidence substantially sharpens the conclusion for USP7 and confirms that the main EGFR-amplification claim is not supported. H4 tested whether EGFR amplification is associated with stronger EGFR dependency. The discovery result was already weak: the signed estimate was only +0.025 and its lower bound touched zero. Independent validation is essentially null, with a signed estimate of +0.0015 and an independent interval spanning both sides of zero. There is no reproducible evidence of a clinically meaningful EGFR-dependency effect in this dataset, so I reject H4 and close it. This is a negative conclusion for the registered EGFR-amplification contrast, not proof that EGFR copy-number states never affect dependency; amplification may be a poor proxy for functional EGFR pathway activity or may be confounded by co-amplified loci.  H36 tests KEAP1 loss versus non-loss for NFE2L2 dependency restricted to the dominant Avana screen library. Discovery and independent validation are nearly identical, with signed effects of about +0.796 and +0.795 and tight intervals far above clinical relevance. I accept and close H36. This strongly argues that the large KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is not merely an Avana-library artifact within this dataset.  H59 tests TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss for USP7 dependency restricted to higher mutation burden. Discovery gave a signed effect of +0.477, and independent validation gave +0.392 with an interval +0.239 to +0.545. Although the point estimate attenuates in validation, it remains far above clinically meaningful thresholds and in the same direction as the main TP53 wild-type/USP7 association. I therefore accept and close H59 as a robust dataset-level context confirmation. The attenuation is a useful caveat: TP53-loss cells and high mutation burden are biologically heterogeneous, and mutation burden may correlate with MSI, DNA-repair defects, p53 pathway state, aneuploidy, or screening artifacts. Thus the claim is that higher-mutation-burden cells in this dataset still show the TP53 wild-type/USP7 association, not that mutation burden causally amplifies USP7 dependency.  Overall, the accepted main dataset associations remain: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker/higher NFE2L2 dependency; MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency; and TP53 wild-type with stronger USP7 dependency. The USP7 association is now validated both overall and in the higher-mutation-burden context, and the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is validated in the dominant screen library. The next priority is to validate or robustness-test the remaining accepted main effects, especially SMARCA4/SMARCA2 and MSI/WRN, while continuing to explore modification by co-alterations and context."}}

record.narrative: No assessments are due. I am registering three blocks of comparisons for follow-up. First, I will test whether the four strongest accepted dataset associations are robust in technically trustworthy or contextually relevant subsets: high screen quality, non-Avana CRISPR library, and high-serum culture.
